What changed: the request is now "In the Atlas Launch hub that Omar Haddad last updated, add the tag launch-ready to the file 'Harbor Point survey - Whitfield.pdf'." The updater clause is locked inside the fronted hub phrase, adjacent to `hub`, and the file isn't mentioned until the main clause — so there is no grammatical path for "that Omar Haddad last updated" to attach to the file. Condition texts updated to mirror the new phrasing (c2 "In the Atlas Launch hub", c3 "that Omar Haddad last updated"); condition ids, fact mappings, seed, query, mutations, and decoys are untouched, and every decoy walk is unchanged.

Why this fixes it: the reader's file-reading depended on the updater clause trailing the whole file description, where loose comma use let it float up to the file. Fronting removes that structural possibility rather than arguing about comma strictness, and it uses only ordinary colleague wording — no hints or exclusions.
